evidence.proposition: Micron stated that HBM3E die are roughly twice the size of equivalent-capacity DDR5, include a logic interface die, and use a substantially more complex packaging stack that impacts yields, causing HBM to consume more than twice the wafer supply to produce an equivalent number of bits.
evidence.semantic_limit: DOES NOT PROVIDE A NUMERIC HBM YIELD PERCENTAGE OR NAMEPLATE CAPACITY FIGURE

evidence.proposition: Micron reported that HBM3E 12H yield and volume ramp were progressing extremely well and that it was shipping HBM at high volume to four customers.
evidence.semantic_limit: DOES NOT PROVE UNCONSTRAINED HBM SUPPLY

evidence.proposition: Micron stated aggregate industry supply would remain substantially short of memory demand, HBM's 3-to-1 trade ratio further challenged supply, and additional cleanroom space was necessary while cleanroom build-out lead times were lengthening.

Micron stated DRAM bit-supply growth was constrained by cleanroom constraints and long construction lead times, higher HBM trade ratio, higher HBM growth rates, and declining bits-per-wafer growth from node migrations.
